## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The probe accesses the trained NextItNet through a compatibility view, although its constructor parameter is named `model`. Relevant hooks are `item_emb`, `log2feats(sequence)`, and `predict_score(features, items)`; `view.model.itemnum` identifies valid catalog embeddings.

The supplied file does not show backbone internals or final user-representation computation. Diagnosis uses sequence-position features returned by `log2feats`, rather than explicitly extracting a final representation. For left-padded histories, any final readout must use the final nonpadding position.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the view and references to `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata category lookup is used directly; review data and stored histories are unused.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors shaped B × L. The probe converts sequences to NumPy, computes features, stacks positive and negative IDs into B × L × 2 candidates, and calls `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 valid item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the mean to [0,1]. Higher values suggest directional collapse; approximately 0.5 indicates near-zero average cosine similarity.
- **Positive–negative margins:** Evaluates at most ten batches in evaluation mode without gradients. Each margin is positive logit minus negative logit. Higher mean and tenth-percentile margins indicate stronger separation. Lower negative-beats-positive and small-margin rates are preferable; the latter uses margin < 0.5.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts positive and negative item categories separately for low-margin and incorrectly ranked positions, retaining the top 20 categories per group.

# Perturbation & Tests

No sequence shuffling, masking, deletion, or sensitivity tests are performed. Embedding subsampling and supplied negative candidates provide the only sampling variation.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing the six named metrics above. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate an interpretation.

These are training-batch diagnostics, not validation HR@10. Margins depend on score scale and negative sampling. Empty valid samples yield zeros. Category metadata is unavailable under this task, so category lists remain empty. Average cosine similarity cannot establish recommendation diversity or comprehensive representation health.


 ## Search results
Sampled-negative separation does not establish full-catalog retrieval quality: sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation, and very small candidate samples increasingly resemble pairwise AUC ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). A 2024 sequential-recommendation study found that aggregate metrics conceal substantial head/mid/tail differences; negative-sampling choices changed both accuracy and popularity imbalance ([Prakash et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276)). These findings support checking whether large supplied-negative margins coexist with many higher-scoring catalog competitors.

Practical diagnostic proposal: freeze one NextItNet checkpoint per category; select reproducible training-history prefixes with their next observed training item as target. Use causal, left-padded inputs and the final nonpadding feature. Compare supplied-negative margin and pairwise win rate with chunked exact catalog rank: score eligible items, exclude padding and prefix-seen items while retaining the target, and accumulate competitors outranking it using a documented tie rule. Report rank percentiles, training-prefix HR@10, target-minus-10th-competitor margin, and scores/frequencies of the highest-ranked unobserved competitors. Treat these as potential hard negatives, since unobserved does not imply disliked. Cross-tabulate by target training-frequency bands and prefix-length bands, with counts and uncertainty; optionally measure top-10 popularity concentration. This is a proposed application of the literature, not a published NextItNet-specific protocol. Prefix targets may already have influenced training, so results diagnose fitting and competition, not generalization. Keep them explicitly separate from the unchanged host validation HR@10; fit no additional predictor and use no test data.

Recent work supports separating evidence relevance, claim support, and evidence sufficiency. A 2025 protocol labels relevance first, then distinguishes support/refutation from several insufficient-evidence states; its authors report improved agreement from these finer distinctions ([study](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.968.pdf)). Another 2025 rubric explicitly prioritizes acknowledging insufficient references and explaining what is missing ([abstention guidelines](https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-acl.877.pdf)). ACORN (2024) evaluates explanations by separate quality aspects and finds that substituting LLM ratings often reduces human agreement—automated diagnostic annotations need calibration against human judgments ([ACORN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.04818)). These are transferable methods, not a validated Amazon recommendation rubric.

For the twenty training users, an adapted recommendation-level record should contain candidate ID, linked history item IDs/timestamps, exact title/description evidence, label, and uncertainty reason. Annotate separately: specific recent connection; apparent duplication with a named history or recommendation item; explicit textual compatibility support or contradiction; insufficient information. Define recency beforehand. Similar titles support apparent duplication, not confirmed ownership; history interactions do not establish intent or satisfaction. Compatibility requires explicit matching requirements/specifications; missing details warrant abstention. Pilot the rubric, independently double-annotate recommendations, retain original judgments before adjudication, and report per-label agreement, abstention rates, label counts, and uncertainty intervals clustered by user. A 2026 review emphasizes matching agreement measures to annotation design and intended interpretation ([Counting on Consensus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06865)). Treat these annotations as evidence audits, not measured user satisfaction or substitutes for validation HR@10.

---

[NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) uses residual causal dilated convolutions to expand temporal receptive fields without pooling. This makes block-by-position activation patching a plausible diagnostic, although the retrieved literature does not establish a validated NextItNet-specific protocol. [Zhang and Nanda, ICLR 2024](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Hf17y6u9BC), show that corruption methods and evaluation metrics can substantially change localization results; their evidence concerns language models, so transfer to recommendation requires validation.

[Heimersheim and Nanda, 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255), distinguish clean-to-corrupted patching, which tests restoration, from corrupted-to-clean patching, which tests disruption. Proposed adaptation: cache matched histories and patch individual convolutional blocks at selected recent positions, recomputing downstream layers. Measure raw target-versus-fixed-negative score margins alongside validation HR@10; report normalized recovery only when the clean–corrupted gap is substantial.
